_comment: What Sentinel lets a coding agent do in this repo. Patterns are globs matched against repo-relative, forward-slash paths. '*' crosses directory separators, so 'src/*' matches 'src/a/b.py'. Matching is case-sensitive on every platform so the team gets identical results.

paths._comment: deny wins over allow. An empty allow list means 'anywhere not denied'.

protected_paths._comment: Paths the agent may read but should not be quietly changing. Each maps to the verdict for touching it.

dependency_files._comment: Changing what the project depends on is a supply-chain decision, so it gets a human's eyes.

action_verdicts._comment: Baseline verdict per action type, before any path rule is considered.

code_risk._comment: Thresholds and keyword lists for the Code Risk Analyzer. All heuristics, deliberately - see instructions.md #3.

sensitive_paths._comment: Areas where a mistake costs real money or real trust. Matched as globs on the changed file's path.

test_paths._comment: How we recognise a test file. Used by the missing-test heuristic.

source_extensions._comment: Files we expect to be covered by tests. Docs and config are exempt.

ignore_extensions._comment: Assets and docs carry no logic risk, so they are exempt from the sensitive-area keywords. Without this, 'admin/css/widgets.css' gets reported as permissions code purely because 'admin' appears in its path.

thresholds._comment: Tuned to be noticeable but not shrill. Adjust here, never in Python.

norms._comment: This project's own rules for the coding agent, in plain English. A norm with 'patterns' is checked by regex - deterministic, free, offline. A norm with only a 'statement' is judged by the model, because no regex catches 'don't redesign the UI without asking'. Severity is always set here by a human, never by the model: FLAGGED means a human should look, BLOCKED means do not ship. Write these by hand, or run: python -m sentinel.norms.wizard <repo>

rules.statement: Never commit a real API key, token, or password. Read them from the environment or a secrets manager.
Never turn off TLS certificate verification. Fix the certificate instead.
Model identifiers belong in configuration, never inline in code. In this repo that means sentinel/llm.py and nowhere else.
Do not disable a test to make a change pass.
Do not add a new third-party dependency without asking first. The standard library is preferred.
Only change what the task asked for. Unrelated refactors, reformatting and cleanups need their own request.

session._comment: Bounds on the snapshot the watcher takes when it starts. Anything left out is named in the session's meta.json and reported as 'could not check' - never silently dropped.

explain._comment: Token budgets for the Change Explainer. Trimmed diffs are marked as trimmed in the text the model sees, so it is never misled into describing a partial change as the whole one.

model._comment: Which LLM this INSTALLATION of Sentinel talks to. Read only from Sentinel's own config, never from a watched repo's - a project we supervise must not be able to redirect our model calls. Every value here is overridden by the matching environment variable (SENTINEL_PROVIDER, SENTINEL_BEDROCK_MODEL, SENTINEL_AWS_REGION, SENTINEL_AGENTCORE_ENDPOINT, SENTINEL_AGENTCORE_ARN).

git_commands._comment: Matched as substrings against the git command the agent ran, after collapsing whitespace. Listed worst-first in spirit; all matches are reported.
